propositions: A drainer process killed or OOM-reaped between lock acquire and release leaves a 0-byte orphan lock file that is never reclaimed, permanently wedging all future enrichment drains with silent skipped results.

The drain lock has no owner stamp written to the file and no staleness check, unlike the store's mkdir write lock which has both, so leaked locks cannot be distinguished from in-use locks and have no recovery path.
Enrichment stops without visible error signal when a drain is skipped due to a held lock, because the skip is logged at INFO level and returns success to the caller.
The inherited lock_owner staleness machinery must route unrecognised (pre-stamp or torn) stamps to a wall-clock ceiling for drain locks, while preserving legacy behaviour for mkdir locks.

A reclaim attempt must be bounded to exactly one retry with a single second FileExistsError treated as a concurrent drainer win, never looped, to avoid mutual exclusion hazards and keep the fix advisory-lock-level.
